absent: Definitions and numeric values of domain flags and masks beyond behavior referenced here.
Full layouts of domain and group and shared and capacity and root and queue objects beyond referenced fields.
Allocation and initialization helpers for working state and domains and groups and roots.
Topology level table contents and ordering and per level construction details.
Asymmetric claiming and NUMA imbalance adjustment and cluster activation effects.
Static branch objects for asymmetric capacity and cluster activity and their consumers.
Cache topology helpers including low level masks and maximum identity management and cache info layout.
Queue online and offline transitions and deadline bandwidth pool accounting and server layout.
Sysctl dirty set lifecycle and consumers and synchronization.
Group reuse helper and per cpu storage layout and temporary mask ownership.

findings.text: Top level builder validates that the input cpu set is not empty, allocates working state, constructs one domain chain per cpu following topology levels until the chain span covers the input set, assigns last level cache identities by reuse then fresh allocation, checks span sanity, builds groups with a NUMA aware variant for NUMA flagged domains and a regular variant otherwise, initializes sharing and capacities, allocates cache counters, attaches all chains under a read side critical section, enables asymmetric and cluster optimizations when observed, reports whether multiple caches were aggregated, releases working state and returns success or no memory failure.

A cpu without a cache identity first scans siblings sharing its low level mask for a usable identity and adopts the first found, otherwise it allocates a fresh identity, so siblings converge and new caches are detected only when no sibling provides one, with negative one meaning unassigned.

Construction proceeds through allocation, per cpu chain building, span sanity, group building, shared object setup with imbalance tuning, capacity claiming, cache counter allocation, protected attach, optimization activation and cleanup, aborting to cleanup with failure status on any allocation or sanity or group error.

Attach routine prunes levels that do not contribute by splicing out degenerate parents while preserving shared ownership and child linkage and sibling preference, promotes the parent when the bottom level itself is degenerate while moving cache accounting upward and clearing stale group flags, then emits debug output, moves the run queue to the new root, publishes the new chain, marks sysctl state dirty, defers destruction of the old chain and refreshes cached top pointers.

A domain spanning a single cpu is always degenerate, a domain carrying group dependent flags with more than one group is not degenerate, a domain carrying wake affinity is not degenerate, all other cases are degenerate, and a parent is degenerate relative to its child when the parent alone is degenerate or when spans match and child flags cover parent flags after ignoring group dependent flags if the parent has a single group.

Domains form a parent and child chain with a circular group list and an optional shared object and optional cache accounting, groups link circularly with individual references and point to shared capacity objects with their own references, shared objects are freed when their last reference drops, group lists are walked circularly dropping capacity then group references, and old chains are reclaimed only after a grace period.

Run queue migration detaches any prior root by marking offline when needed and clearing span membership and dropping a reference with deferred free when last, then attaches the new root by incrementing its reference and setting span membership and marking online when active and reattaching fair and extension deadline servers, all while holding the queue lock with interrupts saved.

Bulk attach of all cpus runs inside a read side critical section, queue migration holds the per queue irq saving lock, regular group building requires the domains mutex, bandwidth reattachment holds the bandwidth pool lock, new chain and cache pointers are published with ordered assignment for concurrent readers, ancestor lookup during counter allocation uses protected dereference, and old domains and roots are freed via deferred callbacks.

Cache refresh records the highest cache sharing domain with its first cpu and weight and shared object, derives a share identity from the lowest cluster domain when present else the cache first cpu, records the lowest NUMA domain and the highest packing domain, and records the lowest full asymmetric capacity domain while selecting the balance shared object from that domain only when it owns one else retaining the cache shared object.

Lowest search walks upward from the bottom and returns the first domain carrying the requested flag, highest search walks upward remembering the last domain carrying the requested flag but stops early when the flag is known to be shared downward since higher levels cannot then carry it.

Verbose debug walks the parent chain and checks that each span and its first group contain the attaching cpu, that flags declared as shared with child or parent are consistently present, that groups are present and non empty and disjoint except for NUMA, that the first group matches the child span when a child exists, that the union of groups equals the domain span and that each parent span is a superset, logging any violation as an error and logging a null chain distinctly.

Empty input sets and insane spans trigger warnings and abort the whole build, any group construction failure aborts the whole build, counter allocation failure unwinds all previously allocated per cpu counters, an empty balance mask and a capacity mask mismatch trigger one time warnings, and debug validation only logs malformed structures without repairing them.

NUMA flagged domains receive private overlapping groups derived from child spans with individual balance masks and seeded capacities, built by wrapping the domain span from the starting cpu while skipping covered cpus and unsuitable siblings and descending to a proper descendant when needed, while other domains reuse per cpu group objects in wrapped order accumulating a covered set and finally linking the collected groups circularly.

An overlap balance mask contains only cpus whose sibling has a child and whose child span exactly equals the group span, the capacity object is chosen by the first masked cpu with the first user installing the mask and later users verifying equality, and capacities are seeded proportional to group weight with minimum and maximum at base scale to avoid faulting when domains are malformed.

Descendant selection first moves down while the child span would exceed the target span to find a descendant staying inside, then moves down while child and current spans are equal to skip levels that attach time pruning will later remove.

Unassigned cache identity is negative one, top builder success is zero and failure is negative no memory, overlap builder success is zero and failure is negative no memory, and cache counter allocation reports boolean success with the stub variant always reporting failure.
Group capacities are expressed as multiples of a base capacity scale with newly created overlap groups using one base unit per member cpu and minimum and maximum initialized to one base unit.

Deadline server reattachment does nothing when the server has no attached bandwidth or when the target cpu set is empty, otherwise it adds the server bandwidth to the per cpu bandwidth pool while holding the pool lock.

Full counter allocation creates one counter array per cpu sized by maximum cache identity plus one on the cpu node, locates the topmost cache sharing ancestor, stores the array with its size and a scaled byte estimate only when cache sharing is present else releases the array, while effective bytes scale hardware cache size by domain weight over hardware sharing weight and yield zero when cache information is missing or sharing weight is zero.

Single member cache sharing domains never count as aggregated, otherwise equal weight ancestors are skipped and aggregation is reported when a larger ancestor remains, with the top builder aggregating across cpus into an output flag and separately enabling asymmetric and cluster paths when their flags are observed.
Sysctl dirty helper records the given cpu in a global dirty set when that set exists, allowing later sysctl handling to notice domain changes.

Shared objects not yet published are freed directly while published ones survive through non zero references, and replaced domain chains and replaced roots are destroyed only after a grace period so concurrent readers can finish.
